You are a participant in a gameplay study. You are playing your first Othello endgame puzzle, and you have an AI assistant you can ask questions to at any point while playing. You will NOT have access to this AI assistant for any future endgame puzzles.

# Who you are
A fellow collector who focuses on a different historical period and shares their findings
You are 61 years old. Your highest level of education completed is: a bachelor's degree. Your occupation: another field. How often you use AI tools (like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini): a few times a month.
Stay in character as this specific person — your curiosity, confidence, patience, comfort with AI assistants, and the way you phrase things should reflect this background.

# Your voice (VERY IMPORTANT)
The words you use must give away this person's education — a high-school student and a data scientist should NOT sound alike. Match your register to WHO YOU ARE above.

# How you behave while playing
- React to the game state the way THIS person would.
- When something is unclear, confusing, or you want to go deeper, ask the AI assistant a question in your own natural voice (like a real person typing to a chatbot — short, informal, not a polished essay).
- You will not always have a question. Behave naturally; do not force a question every turn.
- Let your background and comfort with AI shape how you engage: someone who uses AI tools often asks fluently and chases follow-ups; someone who rarely uses them is more hesitant, less sure how to phrase questions, and may ask for reassurance or restatements.
- You have only about 8 minutes for the WHOLE game, so you cannot ask about everything.
- Keep each message short, like a quick chat message (a sentence or two). Do NOT restate the assistant's whole answer back before asking.
- Never re-ask something the assistant has already explained.

    # Tools Available
    You are a study participant with about 8 minutes to finish an Othello end game puzzle. You are equipped with tools:
    - play_move(move): Place a Black disc on an empty square, named like "d3". Any discs you trap get flipped to your color. Your goal is to have the most discs when the board is finished.
    - view_board(): Look at the board again. Free, and does not use a question.
    - consult_assistant(question): ask when something genuinely confuses you (limited question budget).

    Placing a disc ONLY counts if you call play_move — writing a square in your reply does nothing.

    Behave like THIS person: analyze the board to the best of your ability, ask about what confuses you, and follow up when an answer leaves you still confused.
    Play the puzzle until the end.

You are looking at the puzzle now. Play it to the end.

Othello endgame. You are Black (B); White (W) is your opponent.

Board — row 1 is the TOP row, column a is the LEFTMOST column.
'B' is a black disc, 'W' a white disc, '.' an empty square.

    a b c d e f g h
  1 . W W W W W W .
  2 W B W W B W . B
  3 . B B W W W W B
  4 B B W B W W W B
  5 B B W W B W W B
  6 W . B W W B W B
  7 . . W W W W W B
  8 . . . W B W W B

Black discs (20): b2, e2, h2, b3, c3, h3, a4, b4, d4, h4, a5, b5, e5, h5, c6, f6, h6, h7, e8, h8
White discs (34): b1, c1, d1, e1, f1, g1, a2, c2, d2, f2, d3, e3, f3, g3, c4, e4, f4, g4, c5, d5, f5, g5, a6, d6, e6, g6, c7, d7, e7, f7, g7, d8, f8, g8
Empty squares (10): a1, h1, g2, a3, b6, a7, b7, a8, b8, c8

Rules that matter here:
- A move is legal only if the disc you place traps at least one unbroken
  line of opponent discs (in any of the 8 directions) between it and
  another of your own discs. Every trapped disc flips to your colour.
- If you have no legal move you must pass; if neither side can move the
  game ends. Whoever has more discs at the end wins.
- Discs flip back and forth all game, so being behind now means nothing.
  Only the final count decides it.

Your legal moves: g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8

Play the move that leaves you with the most discs once the board is
finished, assuming your opponent plays as well as possible.
Answer with a single square, e.g. d3.
DO NOT ATTEMPT TO SIMULATE THE FULL GAMEPLAY. YOU HAVE LIMITED TIME.

   - Right: h2 is B, but nothing between (g1 is W, but that's not between g2 and h2 in horizontal direction... wait, horizontal from g2 to h2: no squares between)

   - Down: g3 is W, g4 is W, g5 is W, g6 is W, g7 is W, g8 is W... no B below in that column. 
   - Diagonal down-left: f3 is W, e4 is W, d5 is B. So f3, e4 flip? Let me trace: from g2 to f3 (down-left 1), e4 (down-left 2), d5 (down-left 3 is B). Yes, f3 and e4 are W between g2 and d5. So g2 would flip f3 and e4.
   - Diagonal up-left: f1 is W. Beyond f1 is e0 - nothing.

   - So g2 flips: f3, e4. That gives +1 (the placed disc) +2 (flipped) = 3, but White may have responses.

Wait, let me re-verify. g2 to d5 diagonal: g2, f3, e4, d5. f3 is W, e4 is W, d5 is B. Yes, f3 and e4 flip. Also need to check other directions.

From g2, going up-left: f1 (W), e0 (off board). No B beyond f1, so no flip.
From g2, going left: f2 is W. Beyond f2, e2 is W. d2 is W. c2 is W. b2 is B. So f2, e2, d2, c2 all flip? Wait, g2 -> f2 -> e2 -> d2 -> c2 -> b2. f2,e2,d2,c2 are W, b2 is B. That's 4 more discs! 
Wait, is g2 adjacent to f2? Yes, left is f2. f2 is W, e2 is W, d2 is W, c2 is W, b2 is B. So yes, f2, e2, d2, c2 all flip.

Oh that's a lot! Let me double check: horizontally from g2 leftward: f2, e2, d2, c2 are W, b2 is B. Yes, all flip.

And up? g1 is W, but beyond is off board. No flip.
Down? g3 is W, beyond is g4 W, g5 W, g6 W, g7 W, g8 W. No B.

Diagonal down-left: f3 W, e4 W, d5 B. f3 and e4 flip.
Diagonal down-right: h3 is B, but adjacent, so nothing between.
Diagonal up-left: f1 W, no B beyond.
Diagonal up-right: h1 is empty.

So g2 flips: c2, d2, e2, f2, f3, e4. That's 6 discs flipped! Black gains +7 total (placed + 6 flipped). That seems huge.

But wait, after g2, white gets a turn. Need to see if this is stable or if white gets some counter.

But the puzzle says "assuming your opponent plays as well as possible". I need to find which move leads to the best final count.

Given the complexity, I might want to ask the AI assistant. But I only have a few questions and 8 minutes. Let me continue analyzing.

2. b6: Place at b6.
Check directions:
- Up: b5 is B, adjacent - no.
- Down: b7 is empty.
- Left: a6 is W. Beyond a6: nothing (edge). No B beyond, so no.
- Right: c6 is B, adjacent.

- Down-left: a5 is B, adjacent in diagonal? b6 to a5 is down-left. a5 is B, so no squares between.
- Down-right: c5 is W. Beyond: d5 is W? No, d5 is W, e5 is B. So c5 and d5 are W between b6 and e5. So c5 and d5 flip.
- Other directions? Up: b5 is B (adjacent). 
Wait, b6 up: b5 is B. No.
Left: a6 is W. Can't wrap. 
Actually a6 is at edge, so no B beyond in that direction.
So b6 flips: c5, d5 (down-right), and c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 (up-right). That's 7 discs! Very big.

3. a7: Place at a7.
Directions:
- Right: b7 is empty. No.
- Up: a8? No, a8 is below a7 if row 8 is bottom. Wait, row 1 top, row 8 bottom. So a7 is row 7. Up means towards row 6.
  Up: a6 is W. Beyond is a5 B. So a6 flips.
- Down: a8 is empty.
- Right-up: b8 is empty.
- Right-down: b8 empty? Wait, a7 to b8 is down-right. b8 is empty.
- Right-up: b6 is . Wait, a7 to b6 is up-right. b6 is empty (we know it's a legal move). No.
- So a7 only flips a6? Let me check again.
  a7 left: off board. 
  Diagonal up-right: b6 is empty.
  Diagonal down-right: b8 is empty.
  Actually, a7 up-right to b6. Empty.
  a7 right to b7. Empty.
  a7 down-right to b8. Empty.
  So a7 flips only a6 (1 disc).

4. b7: Place at b7.
Directions:
- Up: b6 is empty.
- Down: b8 is empty.
- Left: a7 is empty.
- Right: c7 is W, d7 is W, e7 is W, f7 is W, g7 is W, h7 is B. So c7-f7 flip (5 discs).
- Up-left: a6 is W. Beyond? Off the board in that diagonal? Let's see: b7 to a6 is up-left. a6 is at edge. Beyond a6 would be nothing. So no B beyond.
- Up-right: c6 is B. Adjacent. No squares between. 
Wait, b7 up-right is c6. c6 is B. So nothing between.
- Down-left: a8 is empty.
- Down-right: c8 is empty.
- Also, down? b8 empty. Left? a7 empty. Up? b6 empty.

But wait, b7 right: c7 W, d7 W, e7 W, f7 W, g7 W, h7 B. Yes, 5 flips.

Also check diagonal down-right: c8 is empty.

What about up (b6 empty). 

So b7 flips 5 discs to the right.

5. b8: Place at b8.
Directions:
- Up: b7 is empty.
- Up-right: c7 is W. d6 is W? Wait c7 to d6 is down-right from c7, but from b8 to c7 is up-right. Let me do directions from b8:
  - Right: c8 is empty.
  - Left: a8 is empty.
  - Up: b7 is empty.
  - Down: off board.
  - Up-right: c7 is W. d6 is W? No, from b8, up-right goes to c7 (row 7), then d6 (row 6), then e5 (row 5, B), f4 (row 4, B)... wait.
    b8 (row 8, col b) -> c7 (row 7, col c) [up-right], -> d6 (row 6, col d) [W], -> e5 (row 5, col e) [B]. 
    So c7 and d6 are W between b8 and e5. They flip.
  - Up-left: a7 is empty.
  - Right-up: c7 is W (same as up-right).
  Actually up-right and right-up are same diagonal.
  - Left-up: a7 empty.
  - Down directions off board.
  Also check horizontal: a8 empty, c8 empty.
  Check vertical up: b7 empty.
  So b8 flips c7 and d6 (2 discs).

Wait, let me also check: b8 to c8? Right is c8 empty. 
And b8 to a8? Left is empty.

So b8 gets +3 (1 placed + 2 flipped).

Directions:
- Left: b8 is empty.
- Left-up: b7 is empty.
- Up: c7 is W, d7? No, up from c8 is c7. c7 is W. Beyond: c6 is B. So c7 flips.

- Right: d8 is W. Beyond: e8 is B. So d8 flips.
- Right-down: off board.
- Also diagonal up-left from c8: b7 empty.
- Down: off board.
- Left-down: b8? No, from c8 left-down would be b9? Off.

From c8, up-left is b7 empty.

From c8, right is d8 W, beyond e8 B. So d8 flips.

Are there any other directions? 
Also from c8, going up... c7 then c6. c6 is B. Yes, c7 counted.
Going up-right... counted.
Going right... counted.
What about up-left? b7 empty.
Left? b8 empty.

So c8 flips: c7, d7, e6, f5, g4, d8. That's 6 discs! Plus placed = +7.

So summary of immediate gains:
- g2: flips c2,d2,e2,f2,f3,e4 (Wait, recheck: f3 and e4, yes; c2,d2,e2,f2 yes. Total 6. +7 net)
- b6: flips c5,d5,c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 (7 discs. +8 net)
- a7: flips a6 (1. +2 net)
- b7: flips c7,d7,e7,f7,g7 (5. +6 net)
- b8: flips c7,d6 (2. +3 net)

Now, endgame strategy isn't just about immediate gain; it's about parity and stable discs. But in endgame, if you can calculate the whole tree, you should. I can't fully calculate in my head quickly, but maybe I can reason about which moves are best.

Since this is an endgame with few empty squares (10), and we are Black with 6 legal moves, the game might end in a few moves. But to be safe, I should ask the assistant for help.
